terms.meaning: The way plants make food: glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water, using sunlight and chlorophyll.
The green pigment in leaves, needed for photosynthesis.
Tiny pores on leaves through which oxygen and carbon dioxide pass.
Thin tubes that carry water and minerals up from the roots.
Thin tubes that carry food from the leaves to all parts of the plant.
A leaf with both green and non-green patches.

items.name: Equation of photosynthesis
items.formula: Carbon dioxide + Water → Glucose + Oxygen (with sunlight and chlorophyll)
items.example: Glucose is then stored as starch in leaves and in parts such as potatoes.

items.name: Testing a leaf for starch
items.formula: Boil in water → warm in alcohol over a water bath → add iodine. Blue-black means starch.
items.example: Alcohol removes the green colour, so the blue-black can be seen.

items.name: Proving light and chlorophyll are needed
items.formula: Only the green patches kept in sunlight turn blue-black.
items.example: The white patches of a variegated leaf do not, and neither does a plant kept in the dark.

items.name: Proving carbon dioxide is needed
items.formula: Half a leaf is kept in a bottle with caustic soda, which absorbs carbon dioxide. That half makes no starch.
items.example: The half outside the bottle turns blue-black. The half inside does not.

items.name: Proving oxygen is released
items.formula: A water plant in sunlight gives off bubbles of a gas that makes a burning matchstick flare up.
items.example: No bubbles appear in the dark.

items.name: Red, violet and brown leaves
items.formula: They also have chlorophyll and make food. Other pigments hide the green.
items.example: The iodine test still shows starch in them.

items.name: Twig in coloured water
items.formula: Water rises through the xylem, so the veins and white petals turn red.
items.example: The colour shows the path that water takes.

items.name: Food in storage parts
items.formula: Phloem brings food from the leaves to the roots, fruits, seeds and tubers.
items.example: A potato stores food that came from the leaves.

items.name: Equation of plant respiration
items.formula: Glucose + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy
items.example: It is the same reaction as in animals.

items.name: Germinating seeds
items.formula: They give off carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.
items.example: Soaked moong seeds kept in a closed flask show this.

items.name: Bottle garden
items.formula: Gases are shared: oxygen from photosynthesis goes to respiration, and carbon dioxide from respiration goes to photosynthesis.
items.example: A water plant and a snail together in a tube in sunlight.

mistakes.text: Plants do not respire only at night. All parts respire all the time, while photosynthesis needs sunlight.
Do not swap them: xylem carries water upward, and phloem carries food.
Never heat alcohol directly over a flame. Use a water bath.
A leaf that is not green can still make food, if it has hidden chlorophyll.
